newsitem.title: GERMANY: Bunds skip higher in late trade, price data help.
newsitem.headline: Bunds skip higher in late trade, price data help.

text.p: German Bunds and futures flitted to session highs in late Tuesday trade after regional inflation data suggested price pressure remains subdued.
Consumer price numbers for North Rhine-Westphalia showed a 0.1 percent decline in April, bringing the year-on-year rate down to 1.6 percent from 1.8 percent in March.
The June DTB Bund futures contract, which had been trading in the 100.50 area, was quoted at 100.60 by 1450 GMT, just off its session high of 100.63.
The benchmark 10-year cash Bund was at 100.94 by the same time, yielding 5.860 percent.

"After dithering around for most of the early part of the session, the market was rallied quite well this afternoon," said one London-based trader. "The price data from North Rhine Westphalia was the main thrust for that."
Pan-German consumer price numbers for April are expected to be released on Friday.
Analysts said the market had experienced a few difficulties earlier in the day with the launch of a new 10-year government bond, with demand not as strong as had been hoped.
The Bundesbank sold 5.0 billion marks in a first trance of the new issue, priced at 101.45 for a 5.80 percent yield.
On international debt spreads, the German market did well against European high-yielders and the U.S. Treasuries.
The 10-year T-note/Bund yield gap puffed out to 113 basis points from 108 at Monday's close, while the spread to Italian BTPs also widened to 180 basis points from 175 previously.
